title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (v11)
author: Asha Patel
summary: Comprehensive product document for Unified Inference v11: overview, PRD, design decisions, roadmap and pricing. Guides engineering and GTM teams through requirements, rollout plan, and release notes.
body:
Summary
-------
This document consolidates the product overview, prioritized requirements (PRD), high-level design specs, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for Unified Inference v11. It is intended for product, engineering, solutions, and sales teams preparing for the v11 release and upcoming go-to-market activities.

1) Product overview
-------------------
What: Unified Inference is Redwood's unified runtime and API that provides predictable, low-latency LLM inference across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments. v11 focuses on advanced model routing, cost-aware fallbacks, and a simplified pricing model for mixed deployment customers.

Why now: Customers are deploying heterogeneous models and hardware and need consistent SLAs, cost transparency, and automated fallback behavior during capacity constraints. v11 addresses operational complexity and improves unit economics while reducing the risk of quality regressions during model switchovers.

Primary users / personas
- ML/infra engineers: need deterministic latency and throughput across environments
- Platform teams: need standard routing, rollout controls and observability
- Product engineers: need simple API and pricing that keeps inference predictable

Value props in v11
- Cost-aware routing: route requests to lower-cost compatible variants when available, with explicit quality deltas
- Canary-aware fallbacks: A/B / canary rollouts across model variants with automatic rollback on quality regressions
- Unified billing simplification: consolidated pricing tiers for mixed hosted/dedicated/private usage with clearer volume discounts
- Developer ergonomics: new SDK helpers and examples for model pinning and routing policies

2) Goals and non-goals
----------------------
Goals (v11):
1. Deliver cost-aware, policy-driven model routing with deterministic SLOs (p95 latency targets)
2. Provide rollout tools to perform canary and staged model rollouts with automatic quality checks
3. Simplify pricing for mixed deployments (hosted + dedicated + private) with clear cost signals
4. Ship developer-facing SDK helpers and console UX for routing policy configuration

Non-goals (v11):
- Full multi-cloud private plane orchestration (out of scope: targeted for v12)
- Support for experimental model compression workflows beyond curated quantization profiles

3) Requirements (PRD)
---------------------
Top-level requirements (MUST):
- R1: Routing policies \u2014 system must evaluate routing policies per request and select a model variant based on latency, cost, and explicit quality budget (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- R2: SLA enforcement \u2014 p95 latency must remain <= 150ms for short-context (<=256 tokens) requests on Hosted tiers under typical load (owner: eng-sre).
- R3: Canary rollouts \u2014 enable traffic splits by percentage and auto-roll forward/rollback based on quality metrics from eval sets (owner: product + applied-ml).
- R4: Billing consolidation \u2014 single invoice line for Unified Inference with breakdown by model/route for transparency (owner: finance-and-legal).

Important but negotiable (SHOULD):
- R5: Expose quality-cost delta estimations in the console for alternative variants
- R6: SDK helper functions for policy definitions in Python/TS

Nice-to-have (COULD):
- R7: Per-customer tunable sensitivity for fallback aggressiveness

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- AC1: End-to-end policy configured in Console + SDK can redirect 30% of traffic to a lower-cost variant while p95 latency changes < 10ms and measured quality delta <= 2% on reference prompts.
- AC2: Billing statement for a mixed deployment customer shows unified line items and reconstructable per-model usage.

Configuration table (example)
- Policy name | Criteria | Primary action | Fallback variant | Weight
- cost-aware-low-latency | cost_delta <= 25% & latency_budget >= 30ms | route | model-q4-8bit | 0.3

4) Design specs (high-level)
----------------------------
Overview:
- The routing decision will be implemented as a policy evaluation layer between API ingress and the model router. Policies will be evaluated using a scoring function that normalizes cost, estimated latency, and quality delta. The router will consult a compatibility matrix (model architecture, tokenizer, max seq) before switching variants.

Components:
- Policy Engine (stateless microservice): accepts request attributes (route, model pin, latency SLO, quality budget) and returns candidate model variants and weights.
- Router: integrates with serving runtime, performs KV-cache-aware warmup when switching variants and ensures token continuity for streaming responses.
- Metrics / quality loop: collects per-prompt quality signals (eval harness) and emits rollback triggers to the rollout controller.

Data flows (sequence):
1. Request arrives at API gateway with route metadata and optional user pinning
2. Policy Engine evaluates policies and returns ranked variants
3. Router selects variant, ensures KV cache compatibility, and forwards to runtime
4. Runtime serves tokens; metrics are emitted to observability and the quality loop

Design constraints and decisions:
- D1: Latency-first fallback: for low-latency routes, prefer models with measured p95 latency within 10% of target even if cost is slightly higher.
- D2: Token-continuity: streaming requests must not experience significant token duplication on variant switches; router must perform prefix-KV transfer where possible.
- D3: Compatibility rules: prevent routing to variants that change tokenizer or max sequence length in a way that would alter user-visible outputs.

Security & compliance notes:
- All policy evaluations and routing decisions are logged with request IDs and customer IDs. Sensitive fields (prompt contents) are redacted in logs per data-retention policy. Private deployments: policy engine runs in customer VPC when requested.

5) Roadmap & themes (quarterly milestones)
-----------------------------------------
Q2 2026 (current):
- Deliver Policy Engine alpha + console UX for policy creation
- SDK helpers for Python & TypeScript (beta)
- Billing consolidation prototype for pilot customers

Q3 2026:
- Canary rollout automation with eval-driven rollbacks
- Quality-cost delta visualizations in Console
- Pilot pricing packages for mixed deployments

Q4 2026:
- Customer-facing GA for routing & rollouts
- Expanded private deployment support for policy engine in VPC
- Additional model variants onboarding and validation pipeline

KPIs / success metrics:
- KP1: 20% reduction in average per-token cost for pilot customers using cost-aware routing (target: 20\u201330%)
- KP2: <1% rate of customer-visible quality regressions during canary rollouts (measured on eval prompt sets)
- KP3: Adoption: 15 enterprise customers using unified billing within 6 months of GA

6) Pricing & packaging guidance
--------------------------------
Objectives:
- Keep per-token economics transparent while enabling discounts for committed capacity across deployment modes.

Proposed pricing tiers (summary):
- Developer (self-serve Hosted): flat per-token pricing with no contractual commit. Includes policy engine (console only) with limited policy evaluations per minute.
- Business (dedicated + hosted mix): discounted per-token pricing (commit tiers monthly), includes full policy engine, routing SLA, and 90-day billing reconciliation.
- Enterprise (Private + Dedicated + Hosted): custom pricing, annual contract, includes VPC-hosted policy engine, dedicated support, and extended observability retention.

Discounts & bundling examples:
- 10% off per-token rate with 3-month commit > $25k/mo
- 18% off with annual commit and dedicated capacity

Billing notes:
- Usage will be aggregated into a single invoice line per customer for Unified Inference. The invoice will contain per-model and per-route breakdowns for reconciliation.
- For dedicated capacity customers, committed capacity overage vs reserved commit should be clearly shown and prorated daily.

7) Rollout plan & operational checklist
---------------------------------------
Pre-launch (2\u20134 weeks):
1. Complete end-to-end integration tests for routing + runtime (ownership: eng-serving-runtime)
2. Run canary on internal workloads and 2 pilot customers (ownership: product + customer-success)
3. Update billing pipeline and Finance QA (ownership: finance-and-legal)
4. Prepare SDK docs, console walkthroughs and sample prompts (ownership: eng-developer-experience)

Launch (week of GA):
1. Enable feature for customers in phased waves (feature flags)
2. Monitor p95 latency, error rates, and quality signals for first 72 hours (SRE oncall)
3. Activate support war room and escalations process (customer-success + support)

Post-launch (first 90 days):
- Weekly QA reviews for pilot customers and monthly QBRs for enterprise customers.
- Iterate on policy defaults and pricing based on observed cost savings and customer feedback.

Incident & rollback playbook (short):
1. Detection: quality loop signals drift above threshold OR SLO violations observed
2. Automated rollback: rollout controller sets traffic back to previous stable variant
3. Postmortem: 72-hour incident review with product, applied-ml, runtime and SRE

8) Release notes (v11 alpha -> GA highlights)
-------------------------------------------
Alpha (2026-03-15):
- Policy Engine alpha released behind feature flag for internal use and selected pilots
- SDK helpers (alpha) published for Python and TypeScript
- Console UX for policy creation (alpha) available in dev consoles

Beta (target 2026-06-01):
- Canary rollouts with auto rollback enabled for pilot groups
- Billing consolidation prototype available to pilot customers

GA (target 2026-10-01):
- Production-ready policy engine, canary automation, and unified billing for customers in supported regions

Known limitations in v11:
- Policy engine limited to model variants that share tokenizer and compatible max sequence lengths
- VPC-hosted policy engine only available in GA (not in alpha)

Appendix: Example CLI and SDK snippets
-------------------------------------
Python SDK (policy creation example)
```
from redwood import RoutingPolicy
policy = RoutingPolicy(
    name="cost-aware-low-latency",
    cost_delta_pct=25,
    latency_budget_ms=30,
    fallback_variant="model-q4-8bit"
)
client.create_policy(policy)
```

Console screenshot notes:
- The policy-creation wizard will show: policy name, primary criteria, simulated cost/quality impacts, and a preview of affected routes.
